annotations.title: CVEs for a product and version

description:
Find vulnerabilities affecting a product across NVD (CPE) and OSV
(package ecosystems), de-duplicated and ranked by priority/EPSS/CVSS.

Distinct products that share a name are kept distinct. If one name maps to
several VENDORS' unrelated products (e.g. "Sentry" → sentry, mobileiron,
apache; "Envoy" → envoyproxy, enphase), the result is flagged `ambiguous`
with `distinct_vendors` — pass `vendor=` to disambiguate. Always check each
result's `match.products` (vendor:product) before trusting a hit.

Distro builds: pass a banner or distro package version as-is ("OpenSSH_9.2p1
Debian-2+deb12u3", version="1:9.2p1-2+deb12u3", "nginx/1.22.1 (Debian)",
"openssh (Alpine 3.20)" + "9.7_p1-r4", "OpenSSH_8.9p1 Ubuntu-3ubuntu0.10",
"nginx/1.18.0 (Ubuntu)"). Each result then also gets `distro_fix`: Debian's /
Ubuntu's / Alpine's own fixed build and, when your build is known, whether it is
past it (distros backport fixes without changing the upstream version, so the
upstream `affected` can say vulnerable on a patched host). Ubuntu banners don't
name the release: `distro_context.release_basis` says how it was placed. Statuses:
fixed / affected / unfixed / not_listed (the distro's record for the CVE lists other
packages, not yours); CVEs the distro settled for your build rank after the rest.

Read with each verdict: `affected.sources_disagree` (records disagree on whether
your version is in range), `affected.ranges_belong_to` (the ranges are a separate
component's own versions, e.g. a provider package: unconfirmed for yours), and a
top-level `truncated` when a big product matches more records than are considered
(exploited ones are always kept).

Args:
    product: product or package name, e.g. "nginx", "Keycloak", "mlflow", "lodash",
             or a server banner.
    version: optional exact version (e.g. "1.18.0", or a distro package build) —
             filters to vulns whose affected range (CPE or package) includes it.
    ecosystem: optional package ecosystem filter, e.g. "PyPI", "npm", "Maven", "Go".
    vendor: optional CPE vendor filter to disambiguate a shared product name,
            e.g. vendor="sentry" (not mobileiron), vendor="envoyproxy".
    limit: max results (default 20).
name: check_technology
title: CVEs for a product and version
